web_title: 7. Why the Price Is What It Is: Valuation, Reverse DCF & Peer Comps
book_title: Chapter 7: Why the Stock Trades Here — Ex-SBC Cash Flow, Dilution & Peer Multiples
question: At $62.84 per share ($15.60B TEU-diluted Enterprise Value), what growth and cash conversion does the market price in once stock-based compensation, a normalized 25.4% tax rate, and the 2026 consignment inventory release are stripped out?

epigraph.quote: Accounting earnings can flatter a leveraged distributor for quarters at a time; true economic cash flow after taxes, stock dilution, and working capital sets the floor.
epigraph.author: Institutional Valuation Desk Principle

web_blocks.title: 7.1 Capitalization Reset: $62.84 Close, TEU Dilution & Real Enterprise Value

web_blocks.html: After an -11.75% weekly drop, BrightSpring closed at $62.84 on November 20, 2026 [18]. Basic quote screens show 198.81M shares, a $12.50B market cap, and a $14.17B headline Enterprise Value [18]. That screen understates true economic claim count. Per Q3 2026 Form 10-Q Notes 7 and 10, basic EPS already embeds 26.2M minimum Tangible Equity Unit (TEU) conversion shares inside 207.0M Q3 weighted-average shares [26]. Adding remaining unconverted TEUs and employee equity awards sets fully diluted shares at 225.0M [6, 26].

At $62.84 on 225.0M diluted shares, pro-forma equity value is $14.14B [26]. Adding Q3 2026 carrying net debt of $1,464.3M ($2,182.1M debt less $717.8M cash) puts TEU-diluted Enterprise Value at $15.60B [26]. On headline Finviz ratios, BTSG trades at 40.81x TTM P/E, 25.29x Forward P/E, 25.57x P/FCF, and 18.80x TTM EV/EBITDA [18]. Against $855M midpoint FY2026 Adjusted EBITDA guidance, TEU-diluted EV/FY26E Adjusted EBITDA is 18.2x [26, 27]. Sell-side targets average $83.44, baking in aggressive FY2027 margin expansion and minimal regulatory drag [15, 18].

web_blocks.title: 7.2 Quality-of-Earnings Adjustments & Normalized Ex-SBC Free Cash Flow

web_blocks.html: Pass 1 forensics revealed three cash-flow flattering items that must be stripped before valuing BTSG [26]. First, 9M 2026 Adjusted EBITDA ($623.0M) added back $91.8M of real costs, including $50.5M of stock-based compensation (~$68M annualized) and $41.4M of integration and restructuring expenses [26]. Deducting $68M of SBC cuts FY2026E Adjusted EBITDA from $855M to $787M of economic ex-SBC EBITDA (19.8x TEU-diluted EV) [26, 27].

Second, Q3 2026 Note 8 shows the 9M effective tax rate fell to 14.4% due to $33.0M of discrete SBC windfalls, versus a 25.4% normalized pre-discrete rate [26]. Third, 9M CFO ($371.2M) received a one-time +$143.4M boost from shrinking on-balance-sheet inventory via $111.6M of off-balance-sheet supplier consignment [26]. Stripping that consignment release, deducting $68M SBC, charging $124M annualized interest ($1.21B floating above $1.0B swaps), and applying a 25.4% tax rate leaves ~$380M of normalized FY2026E ex-SBC FCF (~$1.69/share diluted, or 37.2x P/FCF) [26]. Even in FY2027E, assuming +12% sales, $905M ex-SBC EBITDA, and $65M working-capital absorption, normalized ex-SBC FCF reaches ~$461M ($2.05/share, or 30.7x P/FCF) [26].

web_blocks.the_number: Our conservative 12-month Base Fair Value for BTSG is $65.00 per TEU-diluted share (+3.4% vs. $62.84 CMP), yielding a 12-month probability-weighted expected value of $61.90 (-1.5% vs. CMP).
web_blocks.how_calculated: We blend a 17.8x EV/FY27E ex-SBC EBITDA multiple ($905M x 17.8 = $16.11B EV less $1.464B net debt = $14.64B equity / 225M shares = $65.09) with a 10-year Reverse DCF (10.0% WACC, 3.0% terminal growth) starting from $380M normalized FY2026E ex-SBC FCF.
web_blocks.the_inputs: 225.0M TEU-diluted shares; $1,464.3M Q3 2026 net debt ($1.21B floating SOFR debt); $787M FY26E and $905M FY27E ex-SBC EBITDA; 25.4% normalized ETR per Note 8; $100M-$110M CapEx; -$60M to -$65M normalized annual working-capital absorption excluding one-time consignment release.
web_blocks.the_range: Bear $46.00 (13.0x FY27E ex-SBC EBITDA on IRA/CRUSH compression & SOFR spike; Red Team combined tail stress $38.85 at 12.5x +5% EBITDA less $123.7M consignment/SOFR drag) | Base $65.00 (17.8x FY27E ex-SBC EBITDA / 17.1% 10Y FCF CAGR) | Bull $78.00 (19.8x on $960M ex-SBC EBITDA & 170+ LDD acceleration).
web_blocks.if_off: If Onco360 lifts FY27E ex-SBC EBITDA above $980M while Provider SG&A (+38% in 9M) normalizes and working capital converts without incremental consignment debt, fair value could climb toward $78.00; conversely, a +100 bps SOFR move (-$12.1M cash flow) or CMS CRUSH payment holds pull value toward $46.00—and a combined stress (+5% FY27E ex-SBC EBITDA of $826.4M at 12.5x less $123.7M consignment/SOFR drag) implies $38.85 (-38.2%).

web_blocks.html: Even after last week's pullback to $62.84, the Reverse DCF shows minimal margin of safety once accounting flattery is stripped out [26]. Start from $380M of normalized FY2026E ex-SBC FCF at a 10.0% WACC and 3.0% terminal growth. At $62.84, the market prices in 16.7% annual ex-SBC FCF compounding for ten straight years [26]. Year-10 free cash flow must scale nearly fivefold to ~$1.78B, while GAAP operating margins expand from 3.5% (9M 2026) toward 5.0% [26]. Under a Red Team stress—+5% FY27E ex-SBC EBITDA ($826.4M) at 12.5x less $1,464.3M net debt and $123.7M consignment/SOFR drag—equity falls to $38.85 (-38.2%) [26, 35]. web_blocks.takeaway: At $62.84, BTSG already prices in 16.7% ten-year normalized ex-SBC FCF growth, leaving just +3.4% upside to our $65.00 conservative Base fair value [26].

web_blocks.html: Against live healthcare benchmarks in our November 20, 2026 snapshot, BTSG's valuation looks demanding for its capital efficiency [18, 21, 23]. BTSG trades at 40.81x trailing P/E and posts 7.58% GAAP ROIC on 3.90% operating margins [18]. Why does a COMPOUNDER_PASS business show 7.58% GAAP ROIC? Carrying $3,028.8M of historical LBO and Amedisys/LHC goodwill and intangibles inflates GAAP invested capital ($228.3M of the $238.5M branch deal hit goodwill/intangibles) [1, 26]. By contrast, organic LDD launches (<0.75% CapEx/sales, $28.86 GP/script) earn well above WACC [26]. Meanwhile, oligopoly distributor McKesson (MCK) trades at 27.51x trailing P/E, and Regeneron (REGN) trades at 20.33x trailing P/E [21, 38]. Vertex (VRTX) trades at 33.13x P/E with 20.80% ROE. Eli Lilly (LLY) earns 86.09% ROE and 31.61% ROIC at 44.26x trailing P/E (26.58x forward) [18]. Pure-play home-care peers Option Care Health and Addus HomeCare historically trade near 12.5x–14.0x EV/EBITDA [19, 20].

A sum-of-the-parts sanity check reinforces our $65.00 Base ceiling [26]. Allocating $68M of SBC and $148M of corporate overhead proportionally puts FY2027E economic Pharmacy Solutions EBITDA near ~$760M and Provider Services near ~$145M [26, 27]. Applying 18.0x to specialty pharmacy ($13.68B EV) and 14.0x to home care ($2.03B EV) produces $15.71B total EV [26]. Subtracting $1.464B of net debt yields $14.25B equity, or $63.32 per TEU-diluted share—right around today's $62.84 quote [26]. web_blocks.html: Valuation Re-Rating Trigger: Revisit BTSG only after a reset near $54.00 (~15.0x FY27E ex-SBC EBITDA, below the $56.90 200-DMA) with fresh Stage 1/2 base formation restoring >=1.50:1 asymmetry. Alternatively, reconsider if FY2027E normalized ex-SBC FCF guidance clears $550M without consignment boosts.

web_blocks.title: Valuation Discipline: Why 25.3x Headline Forward P/E Misleads
paragraphs: Headline screens show 25.29x Forward P/E and 25.57x P/FCF, which look fair for +25% top-line growth [18]. Adjusting for $68M annual SBC, normalizing the 14.4% tax rate to 25.4%, and removing the $143.4M 2026 consignment inventory release reveals a business trading near 37x normalized FY26E ex-SBC FCF [26]. Without a deeper price discount, equity buyers hold zero valuation cushion.

book_paragraphs: With BrightSpring's business audit and forensic footnotes locked down in Chapters 1 through 6, we can finally open the live market ledger for November 20, 2026. The stock closed at $62.84, down 11.75% over the past week. At first glance, that sharp pullback looks tempting. Basic quote screens show a $12.50 billion market cap, 25.29x forward earnings, and 25.57x free cash flow for a specialty pharmacy growing sales above 25%. Wall Street's analyst targets still average $83.44.

Before trusting those headline multiples, we have to rebuild BrightSpring's valuation from the ground up using the forensic reality we uncovered in Pass 1. Start with the true share count. Basic quote screens divide the market cap by 198.81 million basic shares. Yet Note 7 and Note 10 of the Q3 2026 Form 10-Q remind us that 26.2 million minimum Tangible Equity Unit shares convert mandatorily by February 1, 2027, and employee equity awards sit alongside them. Counting 225.0 million fully diluted shares puts BrightSpring's real equity value at $14.14 billion at $62.84. Add $1,464.3 million of Q3 carrying net debt, and the true Enterprise Value is $15.60 billion.

Next, strip out the three accounting items that flatter 2026 headline profits and cash flow. First, management guides FY2026 Adjusted EBITDA to $850 million to $860 million, or $855 million at the midpoint. That Adjusted EBITDA adds back roughly $68 million a year of real stock-based compensation—$50.5 million in the first nine months alone—plus $55 million annualized of integration and restructuring expenses. Stock compensation is a real economic transfer to employees and executives. Deducting just SBC lowers FY2026 economic EBITDA from $855 million to $787 million. Against a $15.60 billion Enterprise Value, you are paying 19.8x current-year economic EBITDA.

Second, look at the tax line. Nine-month 2026 GAAP net income benefited from a 14.4% effective tax rate because $33.0 million of discrete stock-compensation tax windfalls flowed through the income statement. Note 8 of the Q3 10-Q states clearly that the underlying tax rate before discrete items is 25.4%. A conservative buyer cannot capitalize one-time tax windfalls as permanent earnings power.

Third, inspect how working capital funded 2026 free cash flow. Nine-month operating cash flow of $371.2 million included a one-time $143.4 million cash inflow from shrinking on-balance-sheet inventories via a new $111.6 million off-balance-sheet supplier consignment program. Consignment frees cash once when you switch terms, not every year forever. When you deduct $68 million of SBC, apply a 25.4% normalized tax rate, charge $124 million of annualized interest on a debt stack that still carries $1.21 billion of unhedged floating loans, and assume normal working-capital absorption as receivables grow, true FY2026 normalized ex-SBC free cash flow drops to roughly $380 million—or $1.69 per diluted share. At $62.84, BrightSpring actually trades at 37.2x normalized ex-SBC free cash flow.

Even if we project a solid FY2027—12% consolidated revenue growth as specialty slows slightly from hyper-growth and Home and Community Pharmacy absorbs further IRA Part D resets—economic ex-SBC EBITDA reaches about $905 million and normalized ex-SBC free cash flow reaches $461 million, or $2.05 per diluted share. At $62.84, that is still 30.7x next year's normalized cash flow and 17.2x next year's ex-SBC EBITDA.

Compare those multiples against our live healthcare peer matrix. McKesson, which runs North America's largest pharmaceutical distribution tollbooth with unmatched oligopoly scale, trades at 27.51x trailing earnings versus BrightSpring's 40.81x. Regeneron trades at 20.33x trailing earnings. Vertex trades at 33.13x trailing earnings with over 20% return on equity. Meanwhile, BrightSpring carries $3.03 billion of goodwill and intangibles, keeping consolidated ROIC at just 7.58% on a 3.90% operating margin. Pure-play peers like Option Care Health and Addus HomeCare have historically traded closer to 12.5x to 14.0x EBITDA.

Run a 10-year Reverse DCF from that clean $380 million ex-SBC free cash flow base using a 10% discount rate and 3% terminal growth. At $62.84, the market is already demanding 16.7% annual free cash flow compounding for a full decade—requiring annual free cash flow to reach $1.78 billion by year ten. That leaves almost no margin of safety if PBM spread compression, IRA Part D negotiations, or CMS's proposed CRUSH audit rules slow growth.

Putting our EV/EBITDA blend, sum-of-the-parts check, and normalized DCF together sets our conservative 12-month Base Fair Value at $65.00 per diluted share—only 3.4% above the November 20 close. Our operating Bear Case sits at $46.00 on a 13.0x multiple if regulatory and rate pressures bite, while our Bull Case sits at $78.00 if LDD launches surge past 170 and Provider SG&A leverage kicks in. Weighting those outcomes 30% Bear, 50% Base, and 20% Bull produces a 12-month expected value of $61.90, slightly below today's share price—and under a combined Red Team tail stress (+5% FY27E ex-SBC EBITDA of $826.4 million at 12.5x less $123.7 million consignment-reversal and +100 bps SOFR drag), downside stretches to $38.85 (-38.2%), pulling expected value down to $59.76. Meanwhile, BrightSpring's 7.58% GAAP ROIC reflects $3.03 billion of historical LBO and Amedisys goodwill sitting in the denominator even though organic LDD launches clear WACC; still, paying 37x normalized ex-SBC FCF leaves zero valuation margin.

Let's walk through the sum-of-the-parts calculation step by step so you can see how fragile the upside cushion is at $62.84. First, separate BrightSpring into its two economic engines and assign each segment its fair share of corporate overhead and stock-based compensation. On an economic ex-SBC basis, Pharmacy Solutions generates roughly $760 million of projected FY2027 EBITDA, while Provider Services generates roughly $145 million.

Even if we award Pharmacy Solutions an 18.0x multiple—a generous premium over pure-play infusion leader Option Care Health—that division is worth $13.68 billion of Enterprise Value. Awarding Provider Services a 14.0x multiple—above Addus HomeCare's historical 12.5x range—adds $2.03 billion, bringing consolidated Enterprise Value to $15.71 billion. Subtract $1,464 million of net debt, divide by 225 million TEU-diluted shares, and you land at $63.32 per share—essentially flat with today's $62.84 market price.

Think also about what happens if interest rates stay sticky around current Treasury yields—with the US 2-year at 4.76% and the 10-year at 5.04%. Because $1.21 billion of BrightSpring's Term Loan B-6 sits floating above its $1.0 billion of swaps, every 100-basis-point rate shock pulls $12.1 million directly out of annual net income and cash flow. Combined with February 2027's mandatory TEU share conversion and KKR's remaining 26.83 million shares, upside toward $83 requires multiple expansion that a 7.58%-ROIC distributor rarely sustains in a tightening market.

Notice one final nuance in our Reverse DCF sensitivity table before moving to the chart. Even if BrightSpring beats our Base assumptions slightly and achieves 17.1% annual ex-SBC free cash flow compounding over the next decade—pushing annual free cash flow from $380 million toward $1.84 billion by year ten—that execution is worth $65.00 per share today. Because shares closed at $62.84, an investor accepting ten years of execution, PBM negotiation, and interest-rate risk earns barely 3.4% valuation upside.

True value investing demands getting paid upfront for operational uncertainty. Until BrightSpring trades at a discount wide enough to survive normalized 25.4% taxes, $68 million of annual stock-based compensation, and steady working-capital absorption, valuation remains a headwind rather than a tailwind.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION: Never Capitalize One-Time Tax and Consignment Boosts
book_callouts.text: When a 25x headline P/FCF screen drops to 37x once you strip out stock-based compensation, a 14.4% tax windfall, and a one-time $143.4M consignment inventory release, the cheap-looking pullback vanishes. Always value repeatable cash flow, never peak working-capital timing.
